The antrun cleanup is now executed at deploy phase instead of process-sources phase. This is because the antrun Dockerfile is also required at deploy phase for push. This is why the cleanup is delayed to the end of the deploy phase.

Patch Set 1:

> Patch Set 1:
> 
> (1 comment)

I'm afraid there might be misunderstanding - there are two options for building these projects:

1. Using Docker environment:
- convenient if user has no Go environment set up
- depends only on Docker engine (common on development machines among ONAP community)
- commands to set it up might get complex: reason to use Makefile #1 (command aliases)
- caching named Docker images can increase development pace: reason to use Makefile #2 (target dependencies)

2. Using local Go environment
- usually common among various Go projects
- uses Go caching mechanisms
- no isolation engine (e.g. Docker) overhead
- short commands with optional arguments (e.g. "go build", "go test")

Makefile targets in sslendpoints for local Go environment would be only command aliases mapping  e.g. "make build" to "go build" or "make test" to "go test" (like https://gerrit.onap.org/r/c/integration/+/104229) so they were intentionally omitted.

Summing up:
1. using Docker for building project is possible but not required (Makefile provided for convenience)
2. using local Go environment is not mentioned in Makefile, but also possible as described in corresponding README sections: Prerequisites/Build (local), Building/Command (local), Running/Command (local) and Testing (https://gerrit.onap.org/r/gitweb?p=integration.git;hb=refs%2Fchanges%2F86%2F103686%2F4;f=test%2Fsecurity%2Fsslendpoints%2FREADME)

You're right that this eventually gets replaced (like discussed in https://gerrit.onap.org/r/c/oom/+/106685)
but it's not 'before' the application reads it, it's done by the lower java layers (javax.net.ssl) that are initialized at startup with SSL certs and that will privilege X509 identity over basic auth (like aaf does).

So the problem is that, portal still tries decrypting that value regardless of it not finally being used. It would take some more work (maybe guilin) to rework portal code to avoid doing that. 

We see this only when trying to sync roles (portal-894) and when that decrypt code is called, I've thought that passing a fake value that has a proper byte length would fool the Cipher class, but it does not.

This check-in is intended to provide Sodium SR3 compatibility of the SDN-R applications. You requested this indirectly via comment to https://gerrit.onap.org/r/c/ccsdk/parent/+/109831.
So the code is mainly adjusting to Sodium and tested with the parent provided by Micha. 
Additionally there was also the action to fix the "check-style" problem that we had. Unfortunately there are a lot of changes because "tabs" are replaced by "spaces". We like to improve here to "not" getting such feedback that to many has changed.

To avoid incompatibility I had to remove to bundles. This bundles are containing yang-tools generated classes. This classes are not compatible between Neon and Sodium. For this reason I had removed the related bundle with all the generated classes. Looks as a big change. But was necessary to provide the requested Neon/Sodium compatibility of the code. This were about 150 deletions. 

This code is tested now with local Sodium builds and the "expected" parents that are provided via CCSDK-2518 and Neon builds. 
The Easticsearch version that you commented is used for a plugin that is doing JUnit tests and is not used in the running Environment. Proposal is to change this version till M1 to avoid hickups.

> Patch Set 1:
> 
> Keeping only symlinks as the markup indicator does not trigger CI on relevant patches (there's no change in symlink). I'll look into this issue

Gerrit trigger in Jenkins spawns a review job based on a file name pattern (there is no file content heuristics or so), in this case where you have no update to the symlinks it won't trigger.

There are only three options:
+ remove symlinks and add suffix to the readme files
+ trigger review job manually (but i'm afraid it won't still validate files as they won't be in review file list)
+ manually add 'verified' flag but this would have to be the case for any further changes to those files (no automatic verification in CI) which is breaking the idea behind introduced rst/md linters.

Personally I'd go with 1st option although I understand your reasoning behind using symlinks you mentioned in https://gerrit.onap.org/r/c/integration/+/109248/5 in reply to my question about symlink.

Implementation of TN NSSMF WF on SO

(1) Workflow of Allocate TN NSSI
(2) Workflow of Deallocate TN NSSI
(3) Workflow of Activate and Deactivate TN NSSI
(4) Workflow of Modify TN NSSI

NOTE:
   1. The full implementation of TN NSSMF consists of two layers:
      (1) The TN Sice definition layer, which is an orchestration
      layer that provides the NBI of TN NSSMF to its consumers
      (i.e., it concerns the "what" question), and (2) the TN slice
      realization layer, which is responsible for the actual network
      configurations of TN slicing (i.e., the "how" question). The first
      layer is done on the SO (i.e., this changeset), while the 2nd
      layer is implemented on the SDNC. That's why this changeset is
      relatively simple, since the "real work" is done by the SDNC.
   2. This changeset depends on the common NSSMF WF
      (https://gerrit.onap.org/r/c/so/+/111477)

This is not the solution of this problem.

The problem is that we get the list of orchestation flows sorted by primary id, not by sequenceNumber.
SequenceNumber defines the order of building block execution.

The problem appears after the following commit:
https://gerrit.onap.org/r/c/so/+/111019

After inserting the ControllerExecutionBB into table, it is on the last record of the table orchestation_flow_reference. 

And that is why when we get the list of bb in WorkflowAction class, ControllerExecutionBB is the last,
but it can not be the last, it must be executed after waitForPnfBB, because this is defined by sequence number.

Here is a solution corrected by me, it is tested on lab and works.

@Sylvain,as Mukesh explained in his email to you...


This is in reference to your review https://gerrit.onap.org/r/c/oom/+/114367/4/kubernetes/so/components/so-vnfm-adapter/resources/config/overrides/override.yaml
 
The Ericsson team has discussed internally about the above hardcoded password. The reason that we put keystore and truststore passwords in the SOL003 Adapter is that the SOL003 Adapter has used its own keystore for communications with bpmn-infra and etsi-nfvo.
 
If we are using the common way of certificates as you are changing, it will break existing communications between bpmn-infra/etsi-nfvo and SOL003 Adapter.
 
As we reported it to you, due to above changes in OOM, we are not able to successfully test the communications around the SOL003 Adapter.
 
Since we don’t have much time to complete our tests for ETSI-Alignment (it used to work but after OOM changes, no), at this time, out team would like to go with the HTTP path instead of HTTPS, as part of this review for Guilin. Another rationale for the HTTP path would be the SO NFVO, SOL003 Adapter and BPMN-Infra are part of SO. > Patch Set 1:
> 
> would it really fix the issue or move it
> you believe that the nexus will trustable from docker hub?

Yes, I think it will fix the problem. According to Nexus documentation, my understanding is that Nexus will act as a proxy and cache for images from docker hub. So the image will be pulled from docker hub only for the first pull attempt towards Nexus for a specific image tag. Once the image exists in Nexus, the image will be pulled only from Nexus.
Further reading here: https://help.sonatype.com/repomanager3/repository-management
However, I dont know if this is the long term solution. Perhaps a local image repository only for CSIT could be considered.  

There are other projects doing the same thing, e.g. : https://gerrit.onap.org/r/c/integration/csit/+/114847

Fix service registration for SDNC

Addresses the inherit race conditions associated with the
BundleActivator abstraction.  From lessons learned in OpenDaylight
project, dependency injection and service injection via Aries Blueprint
is faster, more deterministic, and has better error messaging than
using BundleActivator(s).

This change addresses several aspects:
1) DBLIBResourceActivator is changed to DBLIBResourceProvider.
   This was done in order to imply that this is no longer an
   Activator or subclass of an Activator.  The class is a POJO.
2) DBLIBResourceProvider is split from a single monolithic method
   into several more manageable and better documented methods.
3) Documentation surrounding the resolution of the DB properties
   is added so that a developer can more easily identify the
   strategy (priority) used for resolving properties.
4) dblib-blueprint.xml is added.  This is used to register the
   configuration bean (DBLIBResourceProvider), and pass it as
   an argument to the actual Service (DBLIBResourceManager).
5) Tests are added to test the functionality and resolution of
   the properties file loading.

Fix SDNC service registration

Instead of registgering services via BundleActivator(s), use blueprint
instead.  This change deletes the RecordingActivator, as it was just
used to kickstart the service registration using felix dm.  The idea
here is to instead use blueprint through recording-blueprint.xml.

The decision was also made to register the Service(s) using the
implementation class name instead of the interface class name for
backwards compatibility reasons.  In all reality, registering Service(s)
under the implementation name is less future proof since clients are
no longer able to easily swap in a separate implementation Service.
In the future, we should consider finding usages of this Service and
ensuring that they poll for the interface rather than the implementation.
However, that is separate from this change and is considered future work.

Proposal to remove OSGi dependencies from the CCSDK project

Dependencies on the OSGi frameworks and libraries are removed
by integrating the CCSDK project with the lighty.io.
It's a toolkit that allows to use ODL services (in this case
core services and the Restconf) without the dependency
on the Karaf framework and the Blueprint DI.

In this change are created the lighty.io modules which
initialize and expose same services as the Blueprint DI in
the blueprint.xml files.

Fix service registration for SDNC

Addresses the inherit race conditions associated with the
BundleActivator abstraction.  From lessons learned in OpenDaylight
project, dependency injection and service injection via Aries Blueprint
is faster, more deterministic, and has better error messaging than
using BundleActivator(s).

This change addresses several aspects:
1) DBLIBResourceActivator is changed to DBLIBResourceProvider.
   This was done in order to imply that this is no longer an
   Activator or subclass of an Activator.  The class is a POJO.
2) DBLIBResourceProvider is split from a single monolithic method
   into several more manageable and better documented methods.
3) Documentation surrounding the resolution of the DB properties
   is added so that a developer can more easily identify the
   strategy (priority) used for resolving properties.
4) dblib-blueprint.xml is added.  This is used to register the
   configuration bean (DBLIBResourceProvider), and pass it as
   an argument to the actual Service (DBLIBResourceManager).
5) Tests are added to test the functionality and resolution of
   the properties file loading.

Fix SDNC service registration

Instead of registgering services via BundleActivator(s), use blueprint
instead.  This change deletes the RecordingActivator, as it was just
used to kickstart the service registration using felix dm.  The idea
here is to instead use blueprint through recording-blueprint.xml.

The decision was also made to register the Service(s) using the
implementation class name instead of the interface class name for
backwards compatibility reasons.  In all reality, registering Service(s)
under the implementation name is less future proof since clients are
no longer able to easily swap in a separate implementation Service.
In the future, we should consider finding usages of this Service and
ensuring that they poll for the interface rather than the implementation.
However, that is separate from this change and is considered future work.

Proposal to remove OSGi dependencies from the CCSDK project

Dependencies on the OSGi frameworks and libraries are removed
by integrating the CCSDK project with the lighty.io.
It's a toolkit that allows to use ODL services (in this case
core services and the Restconf) without the dependency
on the Karaf framework and the Blueprint DI.

In this change are created the lighty.io modules which
initialize and expose same services as the Blueprint DI in
the blueprint.xml files.

More info about the lighty.io - https://lighty.io

interaction is removed as PAP directly talks to DB using spring
repository layer. Also the only end result this change brings is that the
'generatedId' alone will be used as the primary key instead of
'generatedId, name and version' together.

Only `neng` [still has issues coming up](https://logs.onap.org/onap-integration/gating/141289-3/infrastructure-healthcheck/k8s-teardown/k8s-teardown/pod-onap-network-name-gen-cb7cd7d45-24c5d-network-name-gen.log) due to running in a java 11 base image.

I gave it a closer look and basically the situation for all services in `ccsdk/apps` is that `neng` and `vlantag-api` are missing the `vintage-engine` dependency and thus were not executing their `junit 4` tests and `sliboot` is running it's test but only has 5.
So long story short is that these insufficient or not running tests made it possible to update the parent to the spring boot 3 one, which broke all those modules.
[I started fixing it](https://gerrit.onap.org/r/c/ccsdk/apps/+/141510) for `neng`, but due to the amount of changes, this is not something that we should rush today I would say.

So my suggestion is to revert the `neng` changes in this OOM CR. We can then run another gating which I expect to be green then.

dbbe49a2490d72d9:
Docs: Add advisory for JSON Pointer errors in OpenAPI specs

Add documentation advisory explaining the JSON Pointer resolution
failure caused by forward slash (/) characters in Swagger 2.0
definition key names.

When migrating from the deprecated swaggerv2doc directive to the
openapi directive, auto-generated Swagger specs from OpenDaylight
YANG tooling contain definition names like:

  ASDC-API/artifacts(config)artifact

The / character is the JSON Pointer path separator (RFC 6901), so
jsonschema incorrectly interprets these as nested paths rather than
flat keys under definitions, resulting in:

  _RefResolutionError: Unresolvable JSON pointer

The advisory documents two fix approaches:
  Option A (recommended): Rename keys, replacing / with .
  Option B: Use RFC 6901 tilde escaping (~1) in $ref values

Also adds a cross-reference from the existing api-swagger-guide.

Ref: https://gerrit.onap.org/r/c/ccsdk/distribution/+/143029

6840bbb02c797eb7:
Expand rendered image name to include sec and ms

Expand rendered image name to include seconds and milliseconds.
This reduces the probability of image name collisions on the cloud
from 1/60 to 1/60000.

The initial change Ic1853ba7566def397b8bce389e2779fe3020c7ce was
reverted, since the change had issues bringing up an instance on the
OpenStack cloud provider. This was because the default `instance_name`
value is taken as the `image_name`, when the instance_name is unset,
the instance_name does not allow FQDN format hostname ending with
a period+number.

The workaround is to use separate `instance_name` parameter in your
builder which does not end with period+number.

Fixed upstream in common-packer [1.].

[1.] https://gerrit.linuxfoundation.org/infra/#/c/10986/

JIRA: https://jira.linuxfoundation.org/browse/RELENG-971

Revert query changes

The changes between patch 3 and patch 4 of this commit
https://gerrit.onap.org/r/#/c/55093, where the parameters
are sent to the SvcLogicContext instead of values, breaks
the save functionality in cdt. When SvcLogicContext is
allowed to subsitute the values, the StringUtils.isEmpty
functions are skipped over.

Although it appears this change is changing a parameterized
query to a static statement query, in fact the query is not
parameterized in its current form either. In its current form,
SvcLogicContext is just subsituting the values into a static
statement query. SvcLogicContext does perform a simple single
quote escape, which could be duplicated here.

bbeb7c9c08255feb:
ECOMP digestion to ONAP

This commit contains features added across previous iteration.
Unfortunatley, its hard to separate out all the features / defect fixes
under the current setup unless an automated ingestion and integration
mechanims is in place.

Following are the details of each feature / defect fix.

- (OPTFRA-347) New Music Response Changes
Required changes for upgrading to music version 3.x

- (OPTFRA-346) Triage Tool Feature Changes
Triage tool for finding out issues with candidates and how they were dropped

- (OPTFRA-280) Order Locking Feature Changes
Orders from SO need to be parked (and later retriggered) in
scenarios where the orchestration of the already given solution
is in progress.

- (OPTFRA-281) Latency Based Homing
This features enables homing based on 'network latency' defined in
has's internally maintained tables instead of plain distance.

Other defect fixes / performance improvements
- AAI Timeout give up change
Defect fix related to dropping candidates when AAI timed out
and didn't retrun within 3 tries. has will now give up in these
scenarios.

- Defect fix replaced all() query with status based query. There was no need to reachout to Music to grab the whole plans
table - we now go only by the value of the status field.

Added the test cases for latency score calculation and added a missing method in utils

Yes it is true that there is a conflict. The main problem is with the camunda-bpm-assert artifact. The latest version 2.0-alpha is based on an old assertJ version: 1.7 which has some API incompatibilities with assertj 2/3. It is possible to use newest version of assertJ, but only in modules that do not require the camunda-bpm-assert depdendency. I've done some cleanup in poms with the assertj artifacts as part of the change https://gerrit.onap.org/r/#/c/72645/.
Basically the main assertj version is 3.11.1, but it is overridden in modules using the camunda-bpm-assert with 1.7.0. This module requires 1.7.0.

Without a --depth 1 option the git submodule update succeeds and with a --depth 1 it fails.   When it succeeds you get older versions of those three submodules published HTML.

I have not had time to confirm the exact cause, but the order of the initial commits on doc repo vs submodule repos could cause this.   There was also a gerrit upgrade that impacted the tracking of submodules for a few weeks of February https://gerrit.onap.org/r/#/c/78448/

I agree shallow clones are more efficient, especially on the ~2 ONAP repos that are large.
I wanted to use depth 1 in the verify job, but Jenkins SCM and/or the JJB scripts do not support the submodule update depth 1.   

I think we want to leave the tox -elocal logic as is detecting a failure on a local test.   

You should continue to use depth 1 for local tests.  

Perhaps we should add a daily documentation test that performs more extensive tests that are expensive or can't be done in a verify job (check HEAD of branch references, validity of URLs, summarizes RST warnings by project, etc).

I will submit a patch to advance the 3 submodule references and add you as reviewer.

Patch Set 13:

Steve: the resolution-key enforcement is out of scope of this patch.

This patch: https://gerrit.onap.org/r/#/c/ccsdk/cds/+/90700/ is addressing it with the following strategy:
There are three existing ways to perform the resolution:
- either we don't store the results at all, whether for resource or template
- either we store using the resolution key. The combination of blueprintName, blueprintVersion, artifactName and resolutionKey has to be unique. If it is re-used, it is considered as a new attempt for that specific resolution request, and process will only try to resolve resources not marked at SUCCESS in the database.
- either we store using the resourceId and resourceType. As previous point, the combination of blueprintName, blueprintVersion, artifactName and resolutionKey has to be unique. If it is re-used, it is considered as a new attempt for that specific resolution request, and process will only try to resolve resources not marked at SUCCESS in the database.
